questions.q:
Explain each EDM term.
(a) loop
(b) build-up
(c) drum machine
(d) breakdown
ms: (a) a sample or pattern repeated continuously
(b) a section of rising tension/energy before the drop (rising pitch, more layers, drum roll, filter sweep)
(c) an electronic device that produces drum sounds and patterns
(d) a stripped-back, quieter section (often without the kick drum) before the music builds again
questions.model: (a) A sample or pattern repeated over and over. (b) The section before the drop where tension rises, e.g. with rising pitch and a faster snare roll. (c) An electronic device that creates drum sounds and patterns. (d) A thinner, quieter section that removes the beat before another build-up.

questions.q: Compare tango and salsa in terms of instruments, rhythm and the way the performers interact.
ms: Tango instruments: bandoneón, violins, piano, double bass (orquesta típica)
Salsa instruments: congas, bongos, timbales, claves, piano, bass, trumpets/trombones, singers
Tango rhythm: marcado (strong marked beats) / habanera rhythm
Salsa rhythm: built on the clave pattern; layered syncopated percussion / montuno piano patterns
Tango: often instrumental, dramatic, sudden stops, portamento, pizzicato
Salsa: call and response between sonero and coro; brass stabs/riffs; improvised section
max 3 if only one style is described
questions.model: Tango is played by an orquesta típica of bandoneón, violins, piano and double bass, while salsa uses a large Latin percussion section with piano, bass, brass and singers. Tango rhythm is based on the strongly marked marcado beat and the habanera, whereas salsa is organised around the clave with layered syncopated percussion. Tango is often instrumental and dramatic, with sudden stops; salsa uses call and response between the sonero and the coro, with brass riffs.

questions.q: Describe the main features of music played by an Arab takht ensemble.
ms: instruments: oud (lute)
instruments: qanun (plucked zither) / nay (reed flute) / violin
percussion: riq (tambourine) / darbuka (goblet drum)
melody based on a maqām
quarter-tones (notes between the semitones)
rhythmic cycles called īqā'āt (dum and tak strokes)
texture mainly monophonic or heterophonic, highly ornamented
improvisation
a wasla: a suite of pieces in the same maqām
context: small group, played in cafés, courts and concerts
questions.model: A takht is a small group of oud, qanun, nay and violin with riq and darbuka percussion. The melody is based on a maqām and uses quarter-tones. The percussion plays rhythmic cycles (īqā'āt) of dum and tak strokes. The texture is heterophonic, with each player decorating the same melody, and there is improvisation. Pieces in the same maqām can be linked into a suite called a wasla.
